thread.title: Ocasio-Cortez withholds support of Pelosi as House speaker | Trump to officiate at Foxconn groundbreaking - MarketWatch

author: Robert Schroeder
title: Ocasio-Cortez withholds support of Pelosi as House speaker | Trump to officiate at Foxconn groundbreaking - MarketWatch
text:
Getty Images Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez celebrates with supporters at a victory party in the Bronx after upsetting incumbent Democratic Representative Joseph Crowley on Tuesday. New York Democratic candidate Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez declined to support House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi for speaker if Democrats take back control of the House.
“I think it’s far too early to make those kinds of commitments right now,” Ocasio-Cortez said Wednesday on CNN’s “Newsroom,” adding that Democrats “need to just focus on winning in November first and then we’ll have the conversation about our leadership.” Ocasio-Cortez delivered a major upset in Tuesday’s primary over incumbent Rep. Joe Crowley, the No. 4 House Democrat.
Also see: Jobs-guarantee idea gets new focus after Ocasio-Cortez victory .
Trump to officiate at Foxconn groundbreaking: President Donald Trump is in Wisconsin Thursday, where he will officiate at the ceremonial groundbreaking for a major Foxconn Technology Group project . As the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports, Trump championed the $10 billion project, which is aided by $4 billion in inducements from state and local governments. He’ll likely label Foxconn a win for his “America First” agenda, the paper says. Foxconn is formally known as Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. 2317, -0.49% and is a supplier to Apple AAPL, -0.15% .
McConnell’s Supreme Court timetable: Moments after Justice Anthony Kennedy said Wednesday that he was retiring from the Supreme Court, Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell vowed that the chamber would act before the midterm elections to confirm a new pick nominated by Trump.
“We will vote to confirm Justice Kennedy’s successor this fall,” McConnell said , as Quote: d by the Hill. Angered, some Democrats referenced Republicans’ decision to block consideration of former President Barack Obama’s pick Merrick Garland. Kentucky Republican McConnell said it was “imperative” that Trump’s nominee be considered fairly.
Also read: Trump’s list of Supreme Court candidates includes senator, judge who has mocked him .
